title: Decent wireless charger
text:
This wireless charger worked well for me. I used it on three different devices (Galaxy S8 - which supports Fast Charging, Nokia Lumia 830, and a Google Nexus 7 - 2nd model from 2013 that supports Qi). All three devices worked well. Positioning on the pad was a little tricky with some devices but overall it wasn't too bad. The indicator lights were convenient but also not distracting because they shut off so quickly which was nice.

The packaging was sufficient and not difficult to open. I wish they included an AC adapter (specifically one that supports the Fast Wireless Charging that this pad supports).

On the Google Nexus I had a thick leather case and that worked fine with the wireless charging. I tried three different cases on the Galaxy S8, a Spigen Neo Hybrid thin plastic one, a Case-Mate Glitter Waterfall case, and a Samsung Clear View case, and all three worked perfectly fine with the Fast Wireless Charging capabilities of this charger (I have had some other chargers fail to charge through the Case Mate, or they do not achieve Fast Charging status with this case).

It also would be nice if it used USB-C rather than Micro USB. But then again I want everything to convert over.

title: My 5th Yootech charger!
text:
This F500 is my 5th Yootech fast wireless charger! I've included my previous review below.* This latest F500 model works just as great as the others! The more obvious physical differences are: The diameter of the F500 is somewhere between the RC200 and the FC600, which has a clear plastic outer ring and is a bit thicker than the other two. The RC200 has a segmented rubber ring on top, which may provide better ventilation. The RC200 also has nice rotating (although dimmer) lights when starting up vs. steady lights on the other two. The FC600 has a USB-C connector vs. a micro USB on the other 2. All 3 models indicate the same amount of time remaining to full charge on my Galaxy S8 and work through an Otter Box Commuter case. This new charger is for my wife's nightstand. We thank you, Yootech!

*The RC200 charger works perfectly as expected -- just as well as the two Yootech FC600 chargers (no longer available) that I purchased last year for my wife's and my new Samsung Galaxy S8s. I liked those chargers so much that I bought another as a gift for my son for letting us join his Verizon Family Plan at Costco where we bought the same 3 new phones together. Our original FC600 chargers sit on a bookshelf in our family room, where they are easy to get to during the day. I put the new RC200 on my nightstand for being close at hand during the night. The highest level of fast charge works with the original Samsung charger and through my Otter Box Commuter case.

My photo shows the FC600, RC200 and F500 chargers in that order.

title: VERIFIED: This charger will fast charge iPhone models 8, 8 Plus and X at 7.5 watts.
text:
If you want to fast charge your compatible iPhone or Samsung phone, this charger will do the trick - provided you follow their directions.

CABLES: The Yootech charger comes with a USB-A to micro USB cable that's engineered to work with the Qualcomm Quick Charge (QC) standards. It's visibly indistinguishable from a legacy cable so you may want to mark it. When it comes to fast charging over USB, most legacy USB cables won't work. Using this Yootech charger and a quality QC compliant power adapter, I can't get it to fast charge with several of my legacy cables. I assume the charger or the power adapter can sense if the cable is compliant or not. Bottom line is you'll need to use this cable or another one that meets the QC standard if you intend to wirelessly fast charge an iPhone or any of the 10W Android phones that the seller lists.

ADAPTERS: An adapter is NOT supplied with the Yootech charger. To support fast charging rates listed, you'll need a QC 2.0/3.0 power adapter rated at 15W or higher. I've tested the following adapters and verified that they'll fast charge an iPhone 8 Plus with the Yootech charger/cable. Please note that the battery needs to be below 80% to fast charge. Above that level Apple apparently switches to a 5W standard charging rate to preserve battery life. I've not had an opportunity to test fast charging at 10W with the listed Android phones.

title: Does Not Charge Reliably
text:
This Qi-Certified wireless charger by Yootech, is nearly useless. A charger is supposed to do one thing, charge a device. In this case, an iPhone. When a charger does that, reliably, every time, it deserves 5-stars. When a charger does not do that, or does it randomly, it deserves 1-star. Logically, there is no in between rating.

These are the issues with the Yootech wireless charger:
1) A protective case that does not cover the iPhone screen makes it nearly impossible to set the phone in a position that triggers the Yootech to start charging.
2) A protective case with a screen cover flap, AND a magnetic closure makes it absolutely impossible to use the Yootech as the magnet in the case interferes with, or confuses the charger. Is that the fault of these cases, or the charger? I think the charger, as magnetic closures on iPhone cases have been around a lot longer than wireless chargers and Yootech should have taken this into account.
3) An iPhone, out of its protective case, does allow this charger to begin charging and sometimes it continues to charge to 100%. However, more than half the time, the Yootech stops charging before the iPhone has a full charge. Sometimes it stops at under 50%, sometimes it makes to to 66% and at others to just over 70%. All these results were for iPhones sitting on the charger overnight, or about 8 hours.

I've had this unit for a couple months, so I cannot return or exchange it. I kept it past the return date, as I wasn't sure if I was making some mistake or the charger was defective. I am now certain this charger, at least the one I received is defective. I DO NOT RECOMMEND this Yootech wireless Qi-Certified charger.

title: So far so good, Charges my phone very quickly, Doesn't work with some bricks adapters
text:
I read a few of the reviews that stated that the charger quit working fairly quickly, but I figured for $15 it would be worth a shot. So far I'm having no troubles aside from the fact that it doesn't want to seem to work with some brick adapters (the little thing you plug into the wall with the USB plug for your phone cable). I plugged the charger into the brick that came with my Galaxy S8 and the wireless charger would cease working after a few seconds, but when I swapped it to the old brick that had come with my Galaxy S7, it started working again right away and hasn't stopped. I'm thinking this may possibly be the issue that some reviewers had regarding the wireless charger suddenly and mysteriously not working within a few days of purchase, but I can't be sure for obvious reasons. I'm not sure why this would be aside from maybe incompatible technology, but a brick is a brick, so who knows? If you do buy this wireless charger, try to use an older brick, not one of the newer ones. If you use a newer brick and the charger stops working, try swapping to an old one before complaining or demanding your money back.
One thing I really like about this is that the light ring around the base lights up when you set your phone on it to signal that your phone is now charging, but the light turns off after a few seconds (Phone continues to charge). It's difficult for me to sleep with light sources in my room and I keep my phone basically right next to my head to make sure I don't accidentally miss my alarms, so this is a god send.
I'll update my review further down the line with more information if necessary, but so far I really like this little charger.

title: Fantastic piece of tech at the right price!
text:
I have a Samsung Galaxy 9+. I have a Samsung wireless charger for it, but I prefer my YOOTECH charger to the brand name one. The Samsung charger requires the phone to sit up on the stand. If you knock or otherwise jar the charger (or whatever it's on) the phone may lose the "sweet spot" for charging.

With the Yootech charger, my phone can lay flat. The "sweet spot" on the Yootech charger clearly let's you know when your phone is in the correct position to charge.

When the Samsung charger completes charging the phone, it turns the backlight on the phone on, then leaves on a green light to signal the phone is charged. This is a. annoying light effect for a dark room. I guess Samsung forgot many of us charge our phones next to our beds.

The Yootech charger emits a quick green circle of light when the phone is charged; after that, the charger goes dark and keeps the phone dark. I greatly appreciate Yootech remembering how annoying it is to have light emitting from electronics in a pitch black room.

The only negative I have for the Yootech charger- it doesn't "fast charge" like the Samsung charger. If I'm charging my phone while sleeping for 6-8 hours, I don't care. Yootech charges the phone during that time period. If I need a quick fast charge, I will use the Samsung charger.

I've had my charger for 6 months, using it daily with no problems. I'd buy another in a minute!!

text:
I love the idea of wireless charging, so I thought I'd get this for a gift to myself and my son. So I ordered and they came as prescribed. Nice look, very simple, plug it in and it doesn't work. Not the pad's fault, but my phone. You see, I have an LG Stylo 4 and my son has a Moto G. Cheap phones, sure, but I did my homework. I initiated a chat session with ATT about both phones. Are they Qi compatible? Her answer? "Yes, they work in the US and Europe" OK, she didn't know what she was talking about, so I spelled it out. "Let me talk to my supervisor!" A few minutes later, "YES, all LG are Qi Compatible for wireless charging!"
She, of course, was wrong. Put the phone on the pad and it blinks at me. Again, the pad is great, the phone and ATT suck.
So I log back on to Amazon and find a QI adapter that says it works on all Android. Right there I should have known better. Android is a OS, not a plug. The adapter I got didn't fit my phone. Boo! It DOES, however, fit my son's phone. Plug it in, put the case back on and BAM, the pad turns green and his phone is charging.
So, great wireless charger. Bad ATT. Bad adapter description. Yay for my son. Boo for me.

I noticed when I first bought it a review stating the charger had burned a ring into their phone case. I was very worried about this but still wanted to try it so I left it on the charger only when I was awake and in the room so I would smell anything going wrong. I'm going to guess that person received a defective unit, which is scary but does happen with any electronics, even Apple branded things. I think we all know it happens with Samsung. Regardless, I've had mine for I believe 3 months now and have had no overheating issues and it charges my phone very quickly. I haven't tested it, but it seems to charge faster than a wire. Again, could be wrong, just my untested observation. I've had no real issues with it, other than the pad being overall kind of small and sometimes you have to poke it a little so it's actually in a charging position. The battery and charger need to be aligned for it to work, naturally. Spending more money on a bigger one would save you those few seconds of potential hassle. Though 90% of the time you just put it down and it starts charging. I would highly recommend this if you just want to test wireless chargers before dropping some crazy amount on a quality one.

Update:
It’s August now, a full 8 months after my initial purchase. Product is still working great and I actually invested in a couple more wireless chargers from this brand because I was so impressed. They have a standing charger that I recommend looking into as well. Anyways, I should note that about a month ago I noticed my phone(on the pad) was hot and the charging pad was hot. Very abnormally hot. So I unplugged the charger and let it cool for a couple days. What I think happened here is that I have moved this charger to my office and I will frequently pick up my phone off the charger to read a text and then put it back. You really shouldn’t continuously remove and replace your phone on any charger, it messes with the battery. I have been better and taking my phone off to check a text and leaving it just on the desk for a bit before putting it back. Being smart with electronics will save you a fire 👍

text: I bought this for the Iphone XS Max and it works well. I didnt spend alot of time looking at these and just kinda pulled the trigger after browsing for 2 minutes so I think there are some things people should know. This is a 7.5 watt charger, this matters as you can buy them  anywhere generally from 5w to 10 w and obviously the higher wattage the faster the charge speed. This doesnt affect me as I generally leave it on the charger over night and its fully charged in the morning. I have left it on the charger during the day for 30 minutes and noticed that it charged roughly 20 percent. I have  a case on my phone and I can still use the charger so no issues there. The charger is small, probably half the size of my phone ( although I do have a large phone) and you have to get the charger on the sweet spot on the phone for it to charge. It isnt hard to align though and you know when its charging because a green light around the edge of the charger comes on indicating that it is in fact charging. A few things I wish I would have thought about before buying a wireless charger are 1. How big the charger is because you dont wanna mess with making sure its charging, you want to just set your phone on the mat and forget about it... a few times I set my phone on the charger not paying attention and woke in the morning to find it wasnt charging at all and having to go through the day with a low battery. 2. It would have been nice to get a upright charger so that your phone could be used as a clock. I dont have a clock in my bedroom and find myself waking up at night, I check my phone to see the time but then have to fiddle with it to make sure its charging again which sucks when you are half asleep, with a upright charger the phone display time can just be displayed without having to even touch the screen just like a normal illuminated wall clock. 3. I would try to find a charger with the most wattage so that it can charge quickly in the event I need it to. Overall this is a great charger but just like with everything as time goes on companies find ways to make things better and I think that is the case here. For me going with a upright wireless charger would have been the way to go.

title: Exactly what I wanted it to be!
text:
I was looking for a wireless charger to keep on my night stand for charging my phone over night. I'm letting it sit there overnight, so I don't need to fast-charge. I just want to set my phone down, and when I get up in the morning it has a full battery. And if I want to check my phone, I don't want to have to unplug it, or have a super long cable so I can use it from my bed.

I have a Pixel 3, and if you want fast-charge for a wireless charger, it has to be from a device specifically approved by Google, and those are all pretty pricey. I was concerned, though, that if I just got some random charger it might make my phone hot, or might damage it if I left it for long hours, or something like that. So I read a lot of Amazon reviews for the lower-cost chargers and settled on the Yootech Wireless Charger; the price was right, and it had all the features I needed (no lights, temperature control, low profile).

I've been using the charger for about a month now, and it does everything I need it to do. I set my phone down, I got to sleep, it's charged when I wake up. My phone doesn't get hot, no change in battery life, it doesn't flash or beep, and it doesn't fall off my nightstand.

The only caveat (which other people have pointed out) is that it doesn't come with a USB wall adapter. This wasn't a problem for me, since I'm drowning in them from other devices, but it's worth being aware of. They're upfront about this, so I don't think it's really even a mark against them.

So, in conclusion, everything is great, and I didn't have to shell out an extra $50 or more for some higher end device that's better than I need it to be!

Charge 2-I put my phone on this charger at 10:00pm at night and my phone was at 30%. Woke up at 6:00am and the charge had made it to 90%. 8 hours got 60% (thats about 7.5% per hour of charge).

This isn't awful but it seems like a very slow rate of charge compared to the plug in charger. I understand that hard wired charges will always charge faster than wireless chargers but 6-7% an hour just doesn't seem fast enough to make wireless charging worth it.

title: For the price a great value
text:
When I purchased my iPhone 8 I wanted to get a wireless charging pad for home. There in the apple store was a product from Mophie. It was easy to just add it on with the total purchase. The one thing that is nice about the Mophie over the Yootech was it did come with the power brick. However that power brick is permanently attached.

While the Yootech is missing the power brick and requires a Quick Charger to function at peak performance the price difference between the two can not be explained by the missing power adapter..

The Yootech is a lot cheaper but is made as well. It is the one that I trust in by backpack with all the stress that entails. I can pull the charger off and hook it up to another cable if needed can't do that with the Mophie. The indication that a positive charging connection has been night is a nice flash from a green light that goes all the way around the device very easy to see. The other product a tiny white light that is completely blocked by anything you place on it.

The YooTech when paired with a Quick Charger adapter will fast wireless charge anything that supports it. When I place my Galaxy S8 (the phone work gives me) on the pad I don't have to fiddle with it it just charges. When I place my iPhone 8 (the phone for me) it just works. And works fast..

When I told people how much I paid for the YooTech they are like what I paid $$$ for x product.

For the price it is a solid product and has functioned well for a year.

Steve

The green LED is also just a nice little feature to know your phone is charging and everything is working as intended.

Overall, great piece of reliable tech so far - hard to go wrong with something this simple but I appreciate good craftsmanship. Great for the price.

I’ve had this product about a month now. The first couple of weeks it worked fine. At least half the time, and close to 75% of the time this week (4th week) it only charges about 30-50%. I rarely charge during the day but always charge while I sleep. I expect to wake up to a fully charged phone and this last week that’s happened only once (I think. Maybe not even once this week).

Now that it won’t charge fully at night I’m forced to charge during the day. I’ll set it up and 2 hours later it will have charged an average of 30% above where I began (plugged in my phone fully charges in an hour). This wasn’t the case in the beginning, it charged as fast as if it were plugged in.

It seems to charge in the beginning and then stop. The daytime charging patterns lead me to believe the same thing is happening at night. At first I thought maybe I was knocking it off it’s connection in my sleep, as it sits on my nightstand, but it’s happened too consistently and during the day when no one is around. I no longer think it’s my error.

Great wireless charger for my iPhone XS. Will definitely purchase another charger as my last iPhone 7s plus had problems with the charging port. I’ll keep one in the kitchen, one next to my bed, and one in my office.
Regarding my 7s plus, the Apple technician stated that over time, particles of debris, dust, and lint can become trapped in the lightening cord port and can cause misalignment of the pins when you plug it in to charge. Had I known, I would have had the port professionally cleaned- but who does that?! So, unexpectedly, I was unable to make or receive any calls. The phone is otherwise completely useful and less than two years old. So I bought a new phone in the meanwhile. Needless to say, I don’t have to use the port on the Xs as often as the X is wireless. The wireless charger makes grabbing my phone to check something seem very painless- I always felt limited with the phone connected to the wall charger. Overall, I love how easy it is to charge and it’s very attractive. My husband just got the 8 and it’s wireless, too. Won’t go back to a traditional charging port.
Sent an email to register for the lifetime warranty and received a quick and friendly response. Nice to know it’s covered for life!

title: Convenient Phone Charger
text: I’ve had my iPhone for a while now and I’ve never thought about getting one of these Qi chargers because plugging my phone in is too easy and it’s just another thing I need. That said, though I’m not sure how well this Qi charger compares to the competition, I like it a lot. It’s really convenient to be able to pick up my phone to use it, then set it back down to charge it up. It’s especially helpful with these new iPhones because like most of you are aware, apple got rid of the headphone port and while that’s not necessarily a negative, I don’t really feel like paying a ton of money for a set of air pods so using the headphone adapter to listen to podcasts and audiobooks at night is really nice. Now, I can also charge my phone while doing that so I don’t have to worry about falling asleep, waking up, and finding my phone, that was supposed to wake me up, dead because I forgot to plug it in. It all sounds like 3rd world problems but honestly it’s the small conveniences in life that make things so much sweeter, this charger is no different. For the price, I’d recommend it, especially since if you get the adapter, you can turn this Qi charger into a 7.5w or 10w charger too which is pretty cool.

title: Easy wireless charging.
text:
I now own two of these charging bases. One is on my nightstand and the other is on my wife’s. Overall they are convenient and easy to use. All that is required is for you to put your phone or ear buds on the bases and allow them to charge. It has been perfect as a nightstand charger because I was going through cables. The constant plugging and unplugging in my phone would eventually damage it. This bases simplifies all that by allowing my to wirelessly charge my devices with damaging the cable or connectors.

Pros:
* simple to use
* relatively small
* lights up when charging connection has been established
* price is right.

Cons:
* no visual indicator of phone is charging once initial light fades. There have been times when I have accidentally knocked my phone slightly and it stops charging. I only realize this in the morning thinking it should be completely charged. It would be nice if a small light or glow was displayed so I could easily see when it was and wasn’t charging without touching my actual phone.
* charging speed seems to be slower than a regular cable.
* nice if initial charging indicator matched the base color. My red base glows green, sales as my black base. It would be nice if it flowed red instead.
* phone needs to be positioned just right for the device to start charging.
* base is a little larger than I would like for traveling purposes.
* doesn’t work with all phone cases and/or phone accessories.

title: Charges so much faster than a regular cord & gives me peace of mind!
text:
This is great for someone who wants a backup charger. I am usually plugged in while using my phone but that’s caused some issues with me going through multitudes of cords. They always fray or the metal prong pulls out and I end up running out at 2am to a gas station praying for an iPhone cord. Enter this handy little charger. I try to put my phone on it at night or if I don’t have a charger that works I put it on there and it charges so much faster than your average cord. Maybe double or triple the time. I keep it in the same place on my bedside table so the cord doesn’t get yanked around keeping the capability of using it viable. This was one of the cheapest models but it definitely works exactly as it should and gives me peace of mind that I will always have something to plus it in.

It comes with the USB cord but NOT the adapter that you plug into the wall. Don’t spend more than a few bucks on one if you don’t have one laying around—they sell them at the dollar store for $1 & are handy to have a few around anyway :-) and if this USB-A cord somehow ends up breaking you can also get one at your local dollar store as a replacement. But it you will probably set it up in one place and not have to move it around or unplug it often and have the cord break so I wouldn’t worry about it. After plugging it into the wall make sure there is no large metal objects directly next to it or underneath it as it will affect its ability to charge. I have mine somewhat close to a fan, however, and it’s caused no issues. Depending on which model you get the light underneath the disc will turn color (green in my case) for a few seconds when you place your phone on it to tell you it’s charging and then turns back off after a few seconds—but I assure you it is still charging. You’ll find it charge extremely quickly comparatively to just a regular cord and it’s been a great thing to have on hand. You can’t use it while it’s charging, however, which is the only main drawback you may find. It works with iPhone 8 and up-however I had luck with it charging an iPhone 6 one time after accidentally placing it on it-but that was an exception not a rule. Only get it it for an IPhone 8 or higher and a Samsung Galaxy/ lS6 Edge Plus/ Note 5 or higher.

It’s a very reasonable price and it’s given me peace of mind knowing I have something that works when my normal cords break due to overuse and constant plugging and unplugging.

This is a rave review, despite the 2nd paragraph!!

I purchased two Qi-chargers for my home, and one as a gift. As recommended, I made sure to use an iPad wall charger for one, and an android wall charger for the other. It does charge slower than wired charging, but is far more convenient. It is small, extremely lightweight, and is excellent for transport/travel.

One of my chargers kept losing connection between the charging cord and the USB port on the device, so my phone wasn’t charging (it would light up green, indicating it was charging, but if the cord or device got bumped, even slightly, it would seem to be working, but would technically be “unplugged”).

Since this item has a lifetime warranty, as indicated on the card which was in the box, I contacted them via FB Messenger. I stated my problem, answered a few questions, snapped a few photos, and in less than a week, had a replacement shipped, free of charge, to my doorstep.

I was not made to feel as though I did something wrong, the customer service representative was very kind and helpful, and I had a wonderful, positive, helpful experience with Yootech. If you’ve read this far, you’re the kind of person who will remember my review and, in the rare event you have an issue, rather than being one of those mad-at-life people who use reviews as an open forum to complain, you will contact the company and have a positive resolution to your issue, too!

title: Very convenient iPhone 8 Plus wireless charger!
text:
I was concerned that the constant plugging in & removing the charge cord would eventually affect the port. My search for a wireless charger found this.

The pros:
+ Pretty good price of $13.99 with free Amazon shipping when I bought this!
+ Much more convenient , vs. a hard wired charger cord!
+ Lots of customer product reviews, 73% 5 star reviews when I wrote this review.
+ Rubberized, nonslip surface that keeps the charging iPhone in place.
+ Advertised - 10W Max fast wireless charging compatible with iPhone.
+ Advertised - temperature control, surge protection, short-circuit prevention.
+ Advertised - 0.47 inch thickness.
+ Advertised - the LED turns on for 16 seconds if the phone is recognized. Once charging has started, the LED turns off for "sleep friendly" operation.
+ Advertised - package contains 1 x Qi Wireless Charger Pad, 1 x 3.3ft Micro USB Cable, 1 x User Manual.
+ Advertised - no hassle 18 months money back/replacement warranty.

The cons:
- The charging appears to take longer, compared to using the hard wired charger cord. ◄ The slightly longer time to fully charge is worth the convenience of wireless charging!
- The supplied 3.3 foot micro USB cable was too short, so we had to source a longer cable.
- Made in China. ◄ For those that prefer to buy products made in the USA.

Closing remarks:
▪ So far, this wireless charger has worked flawlessly. If it continues to work properly, I'll be back to increase my product review.

I placed the phone back on the charger and I looked at how long it stated it would take to fully charge my phone and it said 12 minutes! I could not believe it...12 minutes to get 7%???Nope! I took it off and plugged my wired charger in and it said it would only take 5 minutes to fully chrge! I couldn't do anything except laugh. So I immediately requested to return this piece of useless plastic.

Before I placed the wireless charger back into its box to return it, I gave it one more try. My phone was at 31%; I placed it on the charger and it said it would take well over 2 hrs to fully charge. I took the phone off and plugged my wired charger in and it said it would take a little over an hour. Don't waste your time, energy or coins on this.

The Yootech charger also has a rubber ring around the inside of the circumference to rest the phone on so it is not a hard surface. I have a cover on my phone and it charges very nicely with the cover on. The rubber ring also means the phone does not easily move around on the charger.

I have not had a chance to test it from a low battery, under 50% yet, but I'm sure it will do just fine.

Hard to beat the price, for under $15 it's not much more than a decent charge cable.

This charger is designed for 2 amp (5v or 9v for quick charging) adapters, and the stock iPhone brick (non pro models) is 1A. Using a 1A adapter WILL cause the unit to get hot, which I’m assuming is the issue on some of the “melted” unit reviews. Check your power ratings to make sure they match. If you don’t have a 2A adapter on hand, there’s a version of this product that comes with the correct wall plug.

HOWEVER, when I went to reorder today (May 1st) the price was $12.95 - a 62 percent increase. Seems like price gauging in the age of the Corona virus. Amazon was reported to be watching for this kind of pricing behavior from its providers. Apparently Amazon missed the Yootech Wireless Charger as part of its ongoing review.

title: Best value ever
text:
This was the first Yootech product that I bought, and since then I have fallen in love with their brand. They make fantastic quality products at a very reasonable price. I have seen similar chargers to this one that are much more expensive and don't have the same features this one does.

I LOVE the ring light around it that tells me when the phone is charging. Sometimes, in the middle of the night, I check my phone and then put it back down on the charger, but I rarely get it in the right spot the first time. All I have to do is move the phone around a bit until the green light comes on and I know for sure that it is charging.

The non-slip ring it has on top works perfectly as well. I have yet to have an issue with anything sliding off and I've had this thing for more than a year now. I use it every night for my phone and I've used it to charge my AirPods as well, and both work perfectly.

This is also a great charger to take on the go as well because it's so small that you can literally tuck the thing pretty much anywhere without damaging it. I've also used it with a power bank when I'm out camping or unable to access wall power and it still works without any issues at all, so it really is the ultimate travel charger...(unless you get a power bank that has wireless charging built in...but I don't have the money for those, so I go the "old fashioned" way).

The ONLY thing I don't love about it is the fact that the cord that comes with it is so short. It could use a bit longer cord, but that also depends on where your adapter is and where you're plugging it in. BUT...this hasn't been a HUGE issue for me because I have an extension cord that has 4 USB plugs on it that I just place nearby to where I plan on having the charger, so it works out fine. Just keep that in mind for if you don't have that option for where you want it.

10/10 highly recommend this charger for anyone on a budget. It works perfect time and time again and looks super sleek. I would absolutely buy it again if needed.

I bought this Yootech and a similarly priced Anker for comparison. Both do the job as expected, but I prefer the Yootech over the Anker for two reasons:

2. The LED lighting scheme is better implemented on the Yootech.

On the Anker, a teeny tiny LED light comes on at all times while it's charging. The light is too tiny to see sometimes against the black color of the pad. Then it stays on at all times, which can be bothersome for people trying to sleep next to it.

On the Yootech, the moment you place something on it to charge, a ring of green light comes on and blinks a few times. There is absolutely no mistaking that it's charging as nobody can miss that. Then the green light completely goes out and won't disturb anyone sleeping. See, once I know it's charging correctly, what do I need the light for? Much better thinking here compared to the Anker.

It doesn't light up when the charging is complete. It doesn't change colors. It does the bare minimum of letting you know that charging has successfully been initiated (which is still valuable to anyone who has ever mis-positioned the phone on a wireless charger and come back to a dead phone).

title: Great for the price, lacking in power
text:
This charger works on my note 20 ultra and my iPhone 12 pro, both with a silicon case attached.
The set up is very straight forward.
Its plug and play, it only comes with a USB cable so be ready to look for a spare wall charger or empty port to connect it to.
The bottom of the charger has good rubber feet so slipping isn't an issue.

The charging power isn't so great for short chargers. With my Note 20s fast charger, I can get a full charge in about an hour, but with the wireless charger, a full charge almost triples to about 2 hours and 38 minutes. This was tested from 10% to 100%.

On short charges 20minutes can yield 10-15% while on my fast charger almost 30-40%.

If I leave the phone over night, it's no issue or placing it to charge on my work desk between calls but definitely not something I'm depending on for a quick charge.

I now keep my super charger plugged in in my room and this pad next to my work area for mid day charging.

Overall, a good buy. The product feels well made and definitely not cheaply made. Rubber feet provide good sliding protection. Over night charges are great. Wish it had just a little more power but good for the price.

title: Ideal Bedside Charger!
text:
I have tried numerous wireless chargers and this is the one I like best for overnight charging for one simple but important reason - the indicator light.

An indicator light is important because the phone has to be positioned properly on the charger in order to work. It is an unpleasant surprise when you set your phone on the charger at night only to learn in the morning it was half an inch off center and did not charge over night.

Some chargers do not have indicator lights and you have to look at the screen of your phone to see if the phone is charging, which is less convenient when you are in bed and are setting your phone down to charge on the night stand. That just forces you to sit up to look at it.

Other chargers have an indicator light, but it stays on the entire time the phone is charging. If you like sleeping in a dark room, that can be very annoying.

A few chargers have small indicator lights on the "front" and round chargers (like these most often are) tend to get spun around to where you can't see them.

This charger gets it right. Most importantly, the indicator light on this charger comes on for a few seconds to let you know it is charging, then goes off so as not to be an annoyance. That is exactly what you want next to your bed. And then secondly, the light itself is a band that goes fully around the charger. It is bright enough to see in any light while not being overly bright and blinding in a dark room.

Other than that, this is a charger much like the hundreds of others available. Sure, it doesn't come with the charging brick, but those are pretty ubiquitous these days. I'll take this charger any day over the better known name brands I have tried because the indicator light design is just plain smarter and is exactly what you want for a bedside charger.

I originally thought it was an issue with my phone getting alerts during the night despite being silenced, I tried turning it off and letting it charge while it wasn’t receiving data. That’s when I learned if you have your phone off this base will restart it without you knowing. About 30 minutes after turning off my iPhone and getting ready to sleep, my phone had started flashing along with the base. I ended up unplugging this thing, tossing it in the trash and digging my old plug in charger out of storage.

Another lesson in “you get what you pay for” learn from my mistake and pass this one by.

title: Pixel 4 XL Owners - Look Here
text:
As of Mar '21, it's likely a Google security update that's interfering with your wireless charging.

I exchanged my first wireless charging pad (wasn't aware of the charging issues listed above), so I'm on #2. I'm experiencing the same results.

Prior to the update, this charged at 10.8W (much faster than the 5W advertised). After the update, I had to reconfigure the charging setup so it would charge to full.

Details:

10.8W pre-update = this charger, cable, and any USB C PD charger over 25W. Yay!

10.8W post-update, same config as above, would only charge to 91%. Boo!

Every other configuration of charger, cable, USB A and USB C QC power supply charged between 3W - 5W. Boo!

Before returning your charger, I recommend a web search for the latest info from Google. There may be an upcoming patch that fixes the issue.

The life of a Pixel owner, eh?

title: Excellent alternative to charge cord; essential for moisture sensitive C port Samsung phone
text:
Has worked well and solved a serious problem with my Samsung Galaxy Note 9. This phone often warns "moisture detected" with ominous sounds when I try to plug in the power cord (even though it has not been exposed to water). In this state, the Samsung phone cannot be charged through the C- port. I can make the message go away by placing the phone in the furnace room near the gas furnace (which dries the air in the room), so the C-port is detecting moisture and is triggered by moisture in the air. The humidistat shows 43% humidity (inside and outside temperatures are around 70 degrees in our mild climate).

I have even bought and use a rubber plug (sold as a dust plug to keep out pocket lint) to fit the C-port to keep the port dry. (I attached a short cord to tether the plug to the case, to avoid losing the tiny plug and to keep it handy). Still, if you don’t keep it plugged in, the "moisture" warning will recur.

The Yootech charger (which plugs to USB port) works reliably, and the phone will report the charge percentage and time 'til fully charged, so it replaces the phone's charge cord. Seems to work as fast as the power cord (when the C port allows connection).

Samsung needs to redesign its C-port charger connection, because charging can be a serious problem. All things being equal, I'd avoid buying Samsung phones reputed to have this problem. In the meantime, the Yootech is a great solution.

Have not traveled with the Yootech charger, so no rating, but it should work fine anywhere you have a working USB connector and the right power/voltage.

title: Great! Highly recommended!👍👌  *Tips regarding the pausing when charging
text:
Works great, works great with a case but depends on what type according to manufacturer, highly recommended👍👌

*side note..
Initially I was experiencing similar issues others here are having with the "pausing of the charge".. basically it would be charging for a while and it will stop completely. The unit is NOT defective.
You need to pay attention to the manufacturers specifications and requirements for power requirements as it does not include a adapter.

** the problem is the adapter you are using is likely not giving an output sufficient to power the device.. which is typical for most adapters included with phones and or devices that you are interchangeably using for this wireless charging device.

**solution..
You would need to upgrade to an adapter per the manufacturer's specifications.. I believe it to be at least 2 amps or more.. these are readily available also on Amazon and probably listed as "quick charger adapters" .. prices will vary depending on quality. Obviously I would go with a brand with positive reviews. ( my $.02 as I am not a seller)

I hope this information helps many as I plan to buy another one for use in the office.

title: Good basic charger for the price
text:
I've had this for almost a full year now. It has died about 20 days short of a year. Overall, it is a great little charger for the price. Little weird to to get used to positioning to activate with a case.

To start, $10 is hard to beat for a wireless charger that can charge through basic phone cases. It will NOT charge through thicker cases. Luckily, I use both, so I was unaffected.

The position of your phone is really weird to get used to, but once you find the spot, it lights up green. Also, it is very nice that the green light doesn't stay on the whole time. Especially at night if excess lights can keep you awake and you need your room blacked out.

It really should come with a USB-C cord. Not sure why it wouldn't. Those cords cost next to nothing when mass produced for suppliers.

Would I buy it again? Depends. I'm going to look around at others that may charge faster, come with the USB-C cord, and last longer than a year. I'll have to pay a little more, but we'll see.

If you need a charger asap, or just done want to spend a lot, then this will work just fine.

text:
I will try to be fair in this review, but it will be hard. As the title suggests, I own a Galaxy Z-Flip 3 phone, and bought this charger to have in my living room. I've never owned a wireless charger before, so I don't have any other experience to compare this to. But that's OK, because I never actually got this charger to work.

Whatever coats the Z-Flip3 has a very slippery surface, and this charger has an approximately 8mm wide rubber non-slip circle on both sides. When I plug the charger in, the LED lights green, so it gets power. When I set my phone on the charger it also lights green, and the phone registers that it is being charged.

But for some reason, within less than 5 minutes, the phone just slides off the charger and is sitting beside the charger on the table. I live alone, so nobody else touched it. There were no calls, texts, or alerts. There was no hurricane, earthquake, tornado, blizzard, monsoon, or typhoon. The house wasn't struck by a car.

It doesn't matter how I position it. The table is level enough that nothing else slides around. JUST. THIS. PHONE. So, long story just a little longer, it went in the trash. If you own a Galaxy Z-Flip 3, and are considering this charger, might I suggest that you pick up a package of epoxy as well? You're gonna need it!

I really hate giving negative reviews but I'm afraid I must be honest. I bought this while my phone was giving me that message it shows when there's water in the lightning charging port, as I was afraid my phone would need a wireless way to charge. Thankfully it dried out fine and I can charge it wired or wirelessly, but since I already had this item on the way, I was excited to try it.
This charger arrived really fast and was simple to plug in and use, but it's near impossible to get it to charge my phone for a length of time. It worked for a few hours on day one, but then after a few hours on that first day of use it would randomly disconnect after a few minutes or even moments. If I hadn't been watching it, I wouldn't have even known, since it hadn't been moved at all from its position. I tried removing my (thin) case to place it on again, and the same thing happened.

I set up a return through amazon and got ready for bed, but before I did I tried it one last time and it seemed to connect fine? I figured I'd leave it on there overnight, and consider changing my mind and cancelling the return if the results were promising... but now I just woke up randomly about 3 hours later and checked it, and my phone is so overheated and hot to the touch that it won't even turn on right now. I'm writing this from my laptop as it cools down. :(

I'm really not sure what went wrong with my phone and this product. I'm not a tech expert so idk--maybe its an "Apple making its product unbearably incompatible with other brands' accessories so you'll get fed up and buy their stupid overpriced iProduct" thing, or maybe it's this product itself. Either way I couldn't bring myself to give it one star, but it still really did NOT work for what I needed, so back to the wherever-amazon-returns-go it goes.

UPDATE my phone came back on as I was finishing writing this, and it does say that the software updated automatically, so I suppose it's possible the overheating/unresponsiveness was due to that and I just woke up and caught it at a bad time... but still, I can't recall having issues with my phone getting hot during software update in the past. I'm lowkey scared to give the charger the benefit of the doubt and try charging my phone with it again.

title: Very cheap, works great.
text:
I have 2 phones - a Galaxy S7 and Galaxy S7+. Both work well on this, both of them charge through their cases. Not Otter-Box, huge Vin Diesel cases - just simple cases (they're here on Amazon if you look up "JETech Case for Samsung Galaxy").

Plug it in, set your phone on top. Your phone has to be fairly "centered" on the platform, not hanging too far off one side, or it won't work. There's a green ring that illuminates when you set your phone down so you know your phone is placed properly - if the green ring doesn't turn on, just slightly adjust your phone. The ring shuts off shortly after so it doesn't bother you all night (it's pretty bright).

Charges well, and fast - some days I feel my phones charge faster on this than plugging them in directly (but that's probably just my brain playing tricks on me).

10/10, especially for the price. Recommend it constantly. Other things - it's very small, very lightweight, but there's a rubber ring on the bottom so it doesn't slide all over the place when it's not being weighed down by your phone. There's also a rubber ring on top of course, so your phone doesn't slide around.

I always charge mine face up - that's when a steady green ring comes on, then fades away. When I try charging face down, the green ring blinks intermittently - and that's the only time this thing blinks. I think the pad is confused when you do that...just letting you know in case you were curious.

Oh, been using this thing nearly every day for countless months now. It's handy to have 1 or 2 around your house in strategic areas. No more fumbling for cords. Especially if you drink a lot like me.

Peace ✌

title: Weak Test Results
text:
Going to return the the charger because its weak.
- Samsung Galaxy S9+
- Used Ampere app for measurements
- Samsung brick with Anker cable direct-to-phone connection: ~ 2400mA
- Samsung brick with YooTech cable direct-to-phone connection: ~ 2400mA
- Samsung brick with Anker cable and YooTech wireless charger: ~ 750mA
- Samsung brick with YooTech cable and YooTech wireless charger: ~ 750mA

Summary:
- Both cables were equal in their ability to move power.
- I tested with and without my case (Pelican Shield) and got the very similar results for the wireless charger.

Side note, YooTech charger would NOT charge my Samsung Galaxy watch.

In the end, the difference between 750mA and 2400mA is huge. If the wireless charging was at least 1500mA - 1800mA I probably would have been okay with it. And if it charged my watch, then I definitely would have kept it; but since it couldn’t, then its gotta go. Sorry.

title: Works with a Popsocket (mostly) on my Samsung Galaxy s20 ultra!
text:
I bought this and would have returned it if it didn't work with a popsocket. I use my popsocket more in lieu of a kickstand (so it doesn't need to be perfectly centered) with my phone case (which isn't bulky and certainly not Otterbox bulky). As long as the popsocket is both fully collapsed AND not in the exact center of the phone (which I assume blocks the parts in the phone that allow wireless charging), it WILL work and fully charge. Only real issue is that the popsocket probably makes it more difficult to register and therefore needs to be placed very specifically for it to start charging (one centimeter off that perfect target zone disconnects the charge).

Another thing I noticed is that it doesn't excessively overheat my phone. While the charger itself will get somewhat hot, it's not to a burning degree. And because of where my popsocket is, it makes the phone not rest directly on the charging pad; it instead has the popsocket absorb all of the heat. It also cools down really fast.

Overall, I would recommend this.

The wireless charger is a convenient device that has made my life easier in many ways. I recently purchased the Samsung Wireless Charger Pad, and I have to say, I'm generally pleased with its performance.

The charger is incredibly easy to use. All I have to do is place my phone on the charging pad, and it begins charging immediately. The pad is compatible with a range of devices, including iPhones and Android phones, which is a great feature for households with multiple devices.

The charging pad is also very efficient. It charges my phone quickly, and I don't have to worry about plugging in any cables or finding a wall outlet. The pad is small enough to fit on my desk without taking up too much space, and it looks sleek with its minimalistic design.

One downside of the Samsung Wireless Charger Pad is that it doesn't charge through thicker cases. I have to remove my phone's case in order for it to charge, which can be a hassle. Additionally, the charging pad can get warm during charging, which may be concerning for some users.

Another issue I've encountered with this charger is that it doesn't work well with some USB power adapters. I had to use a Samsung adapter in order for it to charge my phone properly, which can be inconvenient if I don't have the right adapter on hand.

Overall, I would give the Samsung Wireless Charger Pad a 4 out of 5 stars rating. While it has some limitations, it's still a reliable and efficient charging solution that has made my life easier in many ways.

title: Cord is too short. Would not buy again.
text: Power cord is too short. House outlet has to be close. I was hoping to place the charging pad on my dresser but the cord won’t reach the house power outlet. Would not buy again.
